To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
we have developed an efficient gene-driven ENU mutagenesis strategy that allows one to go directly from a gene of interest to mice that carry mutations in that gene.

we have generated a C57BL/ 6J mouse bank that carries thousands of random point mutations, we developed a high-throughput method to screen for mutations in genes of interest, and we developed a protocol to recover mutant mice.

we have developed a gene-driven approach for generating mouse models of human diseases by using ENU mutagenesis, and that we have established a bank of DNA and sperm from ENU-mutagenized mice that can be used to generate mouse models of human disease.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the identification, recovery, and characterization of mutant mice with ENU-induced point mutation(s) in a gene of interest.
the generation of a resource that is valuable to the entire scientific community.
the development of new technologies for the generation, detection, and recovery of mutant mice for functional genomic research.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the CMMB, TGCE mutation screening, and ICSI represent an efficient gene-driven germ-line mutagenesis system for generating mouse models of human disease.
the CMMB represents the largest collection of cryopreserved ENU-induced mutant mice and is an important tool for gene discovery and the generation of mouse mutants.
this is an efficient, gene-driven approach for inducing point mutations in C57BL6/J mice.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the CMMB, TGCE, and ICSI provide a powerful tool for gene-driven mutagenesis and the generation of mouse disease models.
we have produced a large collection of mice that carry point mutations in any of 38 genes of choice, which can be recovered as live animals for further study.
we have developed an efficient gene-driven method for identifying ENU point mutations in any mouse gene.
The main takeaway from our work is that
ENU mutagenesis in the mouse can be used to produce a wide variety of point mutations in any desired gene, which will be of great value for the functional annotation and study of mammalian genes.
ENU-induced mutations in the mouse genome are readily detectable by TGCE, and that the CMMB, in conjunction with TGCE, can be applied to any gene in the mouse genome.
ENU-induced point mutants can be used to study the function of any gene, including genes in the human genome that are inbred in C57BL6 mice.
